issue_context.title: Synology DSM discovery can't be ignored on 0.109.4
issue_context.body:

  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases

  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
In HA Core 0.109.1 I was able to ignore the discovery of my Synology DSM which I have configured in YAML.
Now that I upgraded to 0.109.4 it is back in my notifications and in integrations I am not allowed to ignore it anymore. I also tried to add it to the ignore list in yaml under discovery, but now the error is that it is not an allowed value on top of still notifying me that its available for configuration.

How can I ignore the discovery of my Synology DSM?

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue:  0.109.4
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known):  0.109.1
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv):  Supervised
- Integration causing this issue: discovery synology_dsm
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/synology_dsm/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/discovery/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
synology_dsm:
  - host: !secret synology_dsm_host
    username: !secret synology_dsm_username
    password: !secret synology_dsm_password

discovery:
  ignore:
    - homekit
    - volumio
    - synology_dsm
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.hassio
Source: components/hassio/__init__.py:277
Integration: Hass.io (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 12:26:13 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 12:26:13 PM

Invalid config for [discovery]: value is not allowed @ data['discovery']['ignore'][2]. Got 'synology_dsm'. (See /config/configuration.yaml, line 49).
```

## Additional information
comments: Now that the configuration was imported if you remove the YAML does the issue still exist?

Hey there @ProtoThis, @Quentame, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`synology_dsm`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L389) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

You can remove `synology_dsm` from ignored discovery.

0.109.4 fixes when the integration were discovered multiple times when your NAS is plug with multiple eth.

ok looks like it is resolved after another restart of HA Core. So I guess I was too quick to report this.

This is what it looked like, showing it 2 times.
![Screen Shot 2020-05-06 at 5 10 30 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5417682/81194117-8c60d000-8fbc-11ea-9fca-423a977a4601.png)

Can we reopen this issue? It's not possible to ignore the integration, if you don't want to use it. I have a Synology NAS in my network, but I don't need the integration. The ignore-button doesn't show up:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59510296/81296089-ab6d6980-9071-11ea-9a3a-44ba2e92e5fd.png)

I think it just disappeared at @tinuva , because he is using the integration.
Ups, yes, when fixed #35094 I should still `async_set_unique_id` with the `ssdp.ATTR_UPNP_SERIAL`

@Quentame not sure if it makes sense to post it here or to open a separate thread (if you'd like me to open a new one I can do so and re-close this one), but for multiple releases now, perhaps one or two major ones after you added discovery support, I also see a newly discovered Synology DSM entry which does not have a unique id (so I can't ignore it) even though I already have an existing Synology DSM entry discovered and configured, only have one physical diskstation and no virtual DSMs, and only one ethernet port is enabled. On startup, I'm assuming because of discovery, I see the following error:
```
Logger: homeassistant.components.synology_dsm.config_flow
Source: components/synology_dsm/config_flow.py:143
Integration: Synology DSM (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 1:29:33 AM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 1:29:33 AM
{'api': None, 'code': -1, 'reason': 'Unknown', 'details': 'ConnectionError = <urllib3.connection.HTTPSConnection object at 0x7f4768480940>: Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 111] Connection refused'}
```

I am running HA in a Docker container on my Synology NAS, running the latest version for everything.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7243222/90781860-bbc9ed00-e2cc-11ea-9b55-b60177de3664.png)

When I click "Configure" everything is blank
Ok I opened #42555 because I also still have this issue

review_comments: Isn't the serial number used for the unique id?
Never-mind, its always going to go though `async_step_user` and be swapped out for the serial number before the entry is saved. 👍
Nick is right, the other call to set_unqiue_id is with serial.
we can merge this now I guess, but wouldn't it make sense to always just use mac ?
It is still working as expected because we check for mac in existing entries.

Yep, indeed the SSDP serial is the MAC address (without separators) of the NAS, and I override it to the serial when we succeed to login.

Don’t think it should be nice to use the MAC as unique ID permanently because most of the NAS has multiple Ethernet port, so multiple MAC.
